teaser: Tortured until nearly dead for saying 'One.' He did not give them a single word they wanted. Then he climbed to the top of the Ka'bah and called all of humanity to prayer.
quran_mention: Those who are patient, seeking the face of their Lord — Quran 13:22

layers.title: Who
layers.subtitle: A slave who would not say what they wanted
layers.content:
He was a freedman of Abu Bakr. His kunya was Abu Abdullah. He was born of captives — his mother's name was Hamama. He belonged to one of the Banu Jumah of Quraysh.

Ismail ibn Ibrahim reported from Yunus that al-Hasan said the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Bilal was the first of the Abyssinians.'

Urwa ibn az-Zubayr said: 'Bilal ibn Rabah was one of the victimised believers. He was tortured when he became Muslim to make him recant. He did not give them a single word they wanted. Umayya ibn Khalaf tortured him.'

Umayr ibn Ishaq said: 'When Bilal was strongly tortured, he said: "One! One!" They said to him, "Say what we say." He said: "My tongue will not adorn it."'

They threw him down in the open valley, skinned a cow, and began to say: 'Your Lord is al-Lat and al-Uzza.' He said: 'One. One.' Abu Bakr came and asked why they were torturing this person, then bought him for seven uqiyyas of silver and freed him.
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Bilal was the first of the Abyssinians' — reported from al-Hasan, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: The price of 'One'
layers.content:
Bilal became Muslim in the earliest days of Islam. His conversion cost him everything a man could lose — his freedom, his body, his safety. What he would not lose was the word on his tongue.

Arim ibn al-Fadl reported from Hammad ibn Zayd from Ayyub from Muhammad: 'Bilal's people took him and threw him down in the open valley and skinned a cow. They began to say: "Your Lord is al-Lat and al-Uzza." He said: "One. One." Abu Bakr came to him and asked: "Why are you torturing this person?" He bought him for seven uqiyyas and freed him.'

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'Abu Bakr was our master and our master freed us' — meaning: through freeing Bilal, Abu Bakr freed the Muslim community from something of their own shame.

Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated from Mujahid: 'The first of those who displayed Islam openly were seven: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Bilal, Khabbab, Suhayb, Ammar and Sumayya. Bilal did not give in. He bore it for Allah until they tired of him.'
layers.hadith_ref: Narrated by Arim ibn al-Fadl from Hammad ibn Zayd — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: The voice that called the world to prayer
layers.content:
Al-Qasim ibn Abd ar-Rahman said: 'The first to give the adhan was Bilal.'

When Bilal finished the adhan, he would go to the door of the Prophet ﷺ and say: 'Come to the prayer, Come to success. The prayer, Messenger of Allah.' When the Messenger of Allah came out, Bilal would begin the iqama.

Ubaydullah ibn Musa reported from Isra'il from Jabir that Amir said: 'The Messenger of Allah had three muadhdins: Bilal, Abu Mahdhura and Amr ibn Umm Maktum. When Bilal was absent, Abu Mahdhura gave the adhan. When Abu Mahdhura was absent, Amr ibn Umm Maktum gave the adhan.'

On the Day of the Conquest of Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Bilal to give the adhan on top of the Ka'bah — the slave who had been tortured in its shadow now stood above it, calling humanity to the One. Al-Harith ibn Hisham and Safwan ibn Umayya sat below, watching. One said to the other: 'Look at this Abyssinian.' The other said: 'May Allah force him to change him.' Allah did not.
layers.hadith_ref: Al-Qasim ibn Abd ar-Rahman: 'The first to give the adhan was Bilal' — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Trial and Quality
layers.subtitle: Sabr — endurance beyond what the body can explain
layers.content:
What Bilal demonstrated under torture was not stubbornness. It was sabr — a quality the Quran describes as the capacity to hold firm for a reason the one watching cannot see.

They put a rope on his neck and told their children to tie him between two pieces of wood in Makkah. Bilal was saying: 'One. One.' His torturer Umayya ibn Khalaf is recorded in early sources as saying he had never seen a man who would not break. Bilal broke nothing.

After the conquest, when he gave the adhan on top of the Ka'bah, Abu Jahl's companions — those who had tortured him — were in the crowd below. Mujahid narrated that on the Day of Resurrection, Abu Jahl will ask: 'Where is Bilal? Where are those we counted among the worst in this world? We do not see them in the Fire.' Because they will be in a place his sight cannot reach.

Bilal went to visit a house in Yemen and introduced himself: 'I am Bilal ibn Rabah and this is my brother — from Abyssinia. We were lost and Allah guided us. We were slaves and Allah freed us. Praise be to Allah.' He needed no other introduction. His story was his credential.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 39:10 — 'Indeed those who endure patiently will be given their reward without limit'
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: The adhan lives. Bilal still calls.
layers.content:
When the Prophet ﷺ died, Bilal gave the adhan while he had not yet been buried. When he reached 'I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' the people in the mosque sobbed.

When Abu Bakr asked him to continue, Bilal said: 'You freed me so that I could be with you, then there is a way to that. If you freed me for Allah, then let me go with the One for whom you freed me.' Abu Bakr said: 'I only freed you for Allah.' Bilal said: 'I will not give the adhan for anyone after the Messenger of Allah.' He kept that word.

He went to Syria and stayed there as a fighter in the Way of Allah. Umar asked him: 'To whom shall we appoint your register, Bilal?' He said: 'With Abu Ruwayha. I will never part from him because of the brotherhood the Messenger of Allah established between us.' He was loyal to the brotherhood the Prophet ﷺ had tied even after the Prophet ﷺ had gone.

The adhan he gave — five prayers a day, across every land Islam reached — carries his voice. Every Fajr that wakes the world, every Asr that pauses it — Bilal's 'One' still echoes in it.
layers.hadith_ref: Bilal's words to Abu Bakr after the Prophet's death — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

quiz.prompt: What was the only word Bilal would say when tortured to make him deny his faith?

options.text: Allah
One (Ahad)
Lā ilāha
Muhammad

quiz.citation: Umayr ibn Ishaq, reported in Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: 'One. One.' Two syllables that cost him everything and gave him everything. The word Ahad — the same root as Allah's name Al-Ahad, The One. He was not just refusing them. He was testifying.

quiz.prompt: How much did Abu Bakr pay to free Bilal?

options.text: Three uqiyyas of silver
Five uqiyyas
Seven uqiyyas
Ten uqiyyas

quiz.citation: Arim ibn al-Fadl from Hammad ibn Zayd — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Seven uqiyyas for a man who would give the first adhan of Islam, who would stand on top of the Ka'bah at its conquest, whose voice would echo in every masjid until the Last Day. Abu Bakr did not know this when he paid it. He just saw a man being tortured for saying the truth.

quiz.prompt: Where did Bilal give the adhan on the Day of the Conquest of Makkah?

options.text: From the minaret of the first masjid
From the top of the Ka'bah
From the hill of Safa
Standing in front of the Prophet ﷺ

quiz.citation: Arim ibn al-Fadl from Hammad ibn Zayd from Ayyub — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He who had been tortured in the shadow of the Ka'bah now stood on top of it. The people who had called him 'this Abyssinian' watched from below. Allah had a different plan for Bilal than Umayya ibn Khalaf did.

quiz.prompt: Why did Bilal refuse to give the adhan after the death of the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: He lost his voice from grief
He said he would not give the adhan for anyone after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
Abu Bakr did not ask him to continue
He emigrated to Syria before anyone could ask

quiz.citation: Narrated in the account of Bilal's life after the Prophet — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He gave one last adhan while the Prophet ﷺ was still unburied. When he reached the name of the Prophet in the shahada, the whole mosque wept. He never gave the adhan again. His voice belonged to one person.

quiz.prompt: What did Bilal say when he introduced himself to a house in Yemen?

options.text: 'I am Bilal, the muadhdhin of the Prophet ﷺ'
'I am Bilal ibn Rabah. We were lost and Allah guided us. We were slaves and Allah freed us.'
'I am from the Companions of Badr'
'I am Abu Abdullah, the first to give the adhan'

quiz.citation: Wahb ibn Jarir from Shu'ba — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He did not introduce himself by rank or honour. He introduced himself by his story — lost then guided, enslaved then freed. The same two words that described his life described his gratitude.

quiz.prompt: Bilal said 'One' under torture when saying two different words would have stopped the pain. What allows a person to hold firm to truth when the cost is physical?
quiz.slider_label: How much does your belief cost you right now?

options.text: The pain of betraying yourself is greater than the pain they can give you
You can see something they cannot — and it makes what they do feel small
You stop thinking about the pain and think only about the word
Your love for the truth becomes stronger than your instinct for survival

quiz.citation: Reflection on Bilal's sabr under torture
quiz.scholar_reflection: Bilal's tongue 'would not adorn' a lie. He didn't say he couldn't speak the words — he said his tongue refused to make them beautiful. He experienced his faithfulness as something his body itself would not allow.

quiz.prompt: Bilal stood on top of the Ka'bah and gave the adhan over the heads of the people who had tortured him. What does this reversal mean spiritually?
quiz.slider_label: How do you feel about being vindicated in front of those who wronged you?

options.text: It is the sign that Allah's justice operates in this world, not only the next
It shows that the people who define your worth can be wrong about you
It is a reminder that what looks like the end is often the beginning
It means endurance is not passive — it is preparation for something greater

quiz.citation: Account of the Conquest of Makkah — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The same voice they tried to silence with ropes and rocks and the desert sun — that voice echoed across Makkah from the top of the Ka'bah. The city that had tried to erase him heard him first.

quiz.prompt: Bilal refused to give the adhan after the Prophet ﷺ died. He said his voice belonged to the Prophet alone. What does it mean to keep something sacred by not giving it again?
quiz.slider_label: Is there something in your life you've kept sacred by not repeating it?

options.text: Some things are completed — repeating them would dilute what they meant
His love for the Prophet ﷺ was expressed through the one thing he could withhold
A final adhan for the Prophet ﷺ was his way of saying: you were the reason
Loyalty sometimes looks like absence

quiz.citation: Account of Bilal after the Prophet's death — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He could have continued giving the adhan as an act of worship. He chose instead to make his silence a statement about whom that voice had always belonged to.

quiz.prompt: Bilal was tortured by Umayya ibn Khalaf. When Umayya was killed at the Battle of Badr, it was Bilal who identified his body. How do you understand the relationship between patience and justice in this story?
quiz.slider_label: Do you trust that patience leads somewhere?

options.text: Justice came — but Bilal did not pursue it. It came to him.
Allah's justice does not need you to carry it — your task is only sabr
The one who tortured him was undone by the same war Bilal fought for
All of these — the story contains them all

quiz.citation: Account of Battle of Badr in early Islamic sources
quiz.scholar_reflection: Bilal never raised his hand against Umayya. He said 'One' and endured. At Badr, the men who tortured the early Muslims faced the army that Bilal's 'One' had helped build.

quiz.prompt: Every muadhdhin since Bilal has used the words he used. Every Fajr you have heard was, in a sense, his voice. What does it mean that his act of worship became yours?
quiz.slider_label: How connected do you feel to those who came before you in faith?

options.text: Our worship is not ours alone — we inherited it from those who paid for it
The words of the adhan carry the weight of everyone who said them before
We are linked to Bilal every time we respond to the call
His suffering made the adhan cost something — which is why it means something

quiz.citation: Reflection on the legacy of Bilal ibn Rabah
quiz.scholar_reflection: The adhan was not given by an angel or a scholar first. It was given by a freed slave from Abyssinia who had been tortured for saying 'One.' That is the voice Islam chose to call the world with.
